questions.text: In which board game do players aim to give checkmate?
questions.explanation: Checkmate ends a game of chess.

questions.text: Which Danish toy company makes interlocking plastic bricks?
questions.explanation: Lego is based in Billund, Denmark.

questions.text: How many letter tiles does each player normally hold in Scrabble?
questions.explanation: Players keep a rack of seven tiles.

questions.text: Which game features Colonel Mustard and Miss Scarlett?
questions.explanation: They are suspects in Cluedo (Clue in North America).

questions.text: Which Hungarian-invented puzzle has six faces of coloured squares to twist?
questions.explanation: Erno Rubik invented the cube in 1974.

questions.text: In which country did the board game Go originate?
questions.explanation: Go dates back more than 2,500 years in China.

questions.text: How many pieces does each player start with in chess?
questions.explanation: Each side has eight pawns and eight other pieces.

questions.text: Which doll, launched by Mattel in 1959, was named after the creator's daughter?
questions.explanation: Ruth Handler named Barbie after her daughter Barbara.

questions.text: In which board game do players trade resources to build roads and settlements on an island?
questions.explanation: Klaus Teuber's game was first published in 1995.

questions.text: Which toy, invented by Richard James in the 1940s, can "walk" down stairs?
questions.explanation: The Slinky began as a failed naval spring experiment.

questions.text: Which board game was first designed as "The Landlord's Game" by Elizabeth Magie?
questions.explanation: Magie patented the game in 1904; it evolved into Monopoly.

questions.text: Who invented the Etch A Sketch?
questions.explanation: The French electrician Cassagnes developed it in the 1950s.

questions.text: In which decade was the modern Lego brick design patented?
questions.explanation: The stud-and-tube brick was patented in 1958.

questions.text: Which ancient board game was unearthed in the Royal Cemetery of Ur?
questions.explanation: Boards from about 2600 BC were found by Leonard Woolley.

questions.text: Which company launched the action figure G.I. Joe in 1964?
questions.explanation: Hasbro introduced G.I. Joe as a toy for boys.

spares.text: How many faces does a standard die have?
spares.explanation: A standard die is a cube with six faces.

spares.text: In which game do players try to sink each other's hidden ships on a grid?
spares.explanation: Players call out grid coordinates to hit ships.

spares.text: In which country was the Meccano construction toy invented?
spares.explanation: Frank Hornby invented it in Liverpool around 1898.
